notes: Hand traced from unchanged Chamber_06.jpeg, 1536x1024 top-left pixels, using the full painting, five coordinate-grid zooms and three clean detail crops. Catalog case 6 was compared directly; its large smooth northern contour crossed the Titan and its southeastern contour crossed the lava/cliff.

Only the physically connected west paving and main circular arena are floor. The northern boundary follows observed floor at the fallen arm/hand, the hand-column front/east apron, Titan leg contacts and right fragment. The southern boundary follows the horizontal paving lip, excluding the vertical glowing cliff faces. Visible paving is conservatively continued behind the foreground departure silhouette only as far as the adjacent stone edge supports it.

The lower southwest column platforms, lower foreground Titan foot platform, far right gateway ground and distant right column ruins are separated by lava or cliff. They are not joined by helper bridges. Their separate actual low bases and full painted silhouettes remain occluders where their upper structure overlaps playable paving.

The old exit (1384,726) lies under the foreground gateway architecture with its real foot passage on the isolated lower platform. Exit is moved to the reachable stone approach (1275,740). Return spawn is (1200,711). The old returnExit (215,407) touches the northwest lava margin; the safe connected west approach is (288,415). Entrance remains (365,451).

Fallen Titan collision traces the low underside/root contacts rather than its entire apparent torso, head, horn or hanging cloth projection. The northern floor boundary excludes the inaccessible upper body. The continuous torso/head/horn uses the actual bent-leg support contact; no separate torso-to-floor contact is invented. The arm fingers and fallen forecourt column have concave contact contours, with their high painted silhouettes separate. Small loose gravel and glowing cracks remain walkable; substantial standing rock clusters are individually blocked.

The huge source Titan silhouette is divided into arm/hand, continuous torso/head/horn/bent leg, hanging fragment and detached right fragment to preserve visible concavities and prevent a coarse enclosing hull from hiding actors in empty gaps. Gateway beams use support-ground footprints and separate overhead silhouettes so their openings stay passable in principle.

High confidence: main circular stone court, west approach, cliff lip, foreground fallen column, visible upright column bases and right detached fragment. Moderate confidence: the exact hand-column front apron edge behind rubble, exact underside contacts of the monumental Titan and partial east paving hidden by foreground architecture. Contact uncertainty is about 6-12 px for masonry and 12-20 px for hidden Titan underside. Lower disconnected island footprints are occlusion-only context.

Occlusion probes are three actual connected-floor behind/front pairs outside the physical bases, testing the south standing rock, fallen forecourt column and rear rubble. All navigation anchors, enemies and positive probes require .45 world clearance under the production image-to-ground metric (player radius .38). The hand column has lava and rock behind it, so it deliberately has no behind-column floor probe. No source painting, shared catalog, layout asset or scene is edited.
